sources.cite: Data Programming with Python (course site), Getting started: Kernel State
sources.note: Read 2026-11-17 through a summarizing fetch. Notebook memory 'persists throughout your session based on the sequence of cell executions'; 'You must explicitly re-run all dependent cells'; after a cell is deleted 'The Kernel remembers the temporary_variable ... even though the defining cell is gone'; restart and run all 'perfectly simulates running your notebook from a completely clean slate' and is recommended before finalizing work. A course page about Colab; Jupyter behaves the same way (author's statement).

scoring.modelReasoning: Two people, one notebook, two numbers: the difference is kernel state. Execution counts are out of order and len(df) differs, because a deleted cell filtered the DataFrame and the kernel still holds it. Restart the kernel, run all cells in order, and report that result. Rerunning one cell keeps the hidden state; restoring the filter makes it reproducible but excludes learners the funder counts.
